title: Etiquette & language
body:
As repeat visitors, most of this is probably review — a few things specific to this trip's stops: yatai etiquette is real and locally enforced — don't linger once you're done eating (the bench seat is someone else's queue), and expect cash-only. Ryokan etiquette at Miyamaso Takamiya: yukata provided, wear it loosely left-over-right (right-over-left is how the dead are dressed), no tattoos policy is common at communal onsen baths in older properties — worth confirming directly with the ryokan if either of you has visible ink. Ropeways and gondolas (Mt. Moiwa, Zao) queue in an orderly line; no jaywalking the boarding area.

Language: English signage is solid at stations and chain stores, thinner at small ramen counters, yatai, and rural onsen towns (Zao, Naruko). A translation app with camera-OCR (Google Translate's photo mode) covers menus without English; point-and-show works everywhere. ⚠ No verified phrase card is included — a wrong safety-relevant phrase is worse than none, and situational phrases weren't rigorously bilingual-source-checked. Bring a translation app instead.
